SearchAliases: man hanging from a tree by his teeth
answer and fall from the tree
Senses.Explanation: A person hangs in a tree with the mouth gripping the only supporting branch: neither hand holds a branch and neither foot rests on one. Xiangyan Zhixian's setup places an unnamed person below who asks the meaning of the ancestral teacher's coming from the west. Refusing to answer fails the question, but speaking means releasing the mouth's sole hold and losing one's life. Xiangyan's physical predicament becomes the named 'Xiangyan up the tree' public case. Zhean Jingfan preserves Hutou's counter-question about before the ascent; an impersonal heading numbers and titles the case in Wansong Xingxiu's commentary; Yulin Tongxiu raises it as a public case; Dahui Zonggao examines an unnamed monk with it in an entering interview; a reviewed unnamed monk asks Zongbao Daodu about it and Zongbao answers; and Lingyin Jude Li raises it to test Miaoyun before pressing the before-ascent question. The headword names this case and testing history, not Xiangyan as a separate dictionary figure.
Senses.Note: Zen bends an ordinary climbing scene into a named public-interview case whose demand to answer is explicit. Xiangyan is a lineage master and remains on the roster. The setup without the contiguous title is supporting family evidence; the six exact-title witnesses independently attest the lexicalized case. No second thing is attested.

Occurrences.Kwic: 香嚴上樹香嚴上樹香嚴和尚云。如人上樹。口啣樹枝。手不攀枝。脚不踏樹。樹下有人。問西來意。不對即違他所問。若對又喪身失命
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Gateless Barrier (無門關): the impersonal case heading names Xiangyan up the tree, after which the compiler explicitly introduces the physical setup as Xiangyan Zhixian's speech.

ActorAttribution.ActorLabel: the impersonal Gateless Barrier case heading
ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The exact headword is a repeated title immediately before 香嚴和尚云 introduces Xiangyan's distinct quoted setup.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師問僧：香嚴上樹話，儞作麼生？僧撒手便行。師云：儞擬那裏去那？僧無語，師便打
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui Zonggao, in the Linked Lamps Compendium (聯燈會要), uses the named case in an entering interview, challenges an unnamed monk who walks away, and strikes him after silence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：香嚴上樹話意作麼生？師云：蒼天！蒼天！
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zongbao Daodu (宗寶道獨禪師語錄), an unnamed monk speaks the exact question about the named case; Zongbao answers ‘Heaven! Heaven!’ without repeating the headword. All six attribution rungs leave the questioning monk personally unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 第七則香嚴上樹舉：香嚴垂語云：如人上樹，口銜樹枝，手不攀枝，脚不踏枝。下有人問西來意，若不對，違他所問；若對，又喪身失命

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 第七則香嚴上樹 is an editorial numbered heading before 舉 introduces Xiangyan Zhixian's quoted setup; the title is not a personal speech turn.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Elder Wansong's Commentary on Tiantong Jue's Request Record (萬松老人評唱天童覺和尚拈古請益錄), the impersonal editorial narrator supplies the heading ‘Case Seven: Xiangyan up the tree’ before introducing Xiangyan Zhixian's quoted dilemma. Wansong Xingxiu is commentator and record-owner context; Xiangyan is the quoted setup speaker, but neither is the grammatical actor of the heading.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。舉香嚴上樹話畢，乃曰：「當時有箇虎頭上座出曰：『上樹即不問，未上樹請和尚道。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhean Jingfan, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhean Fan (蔗菴範禪師語錄), raises the named case in a hall address and quotes Hutou's before-the-tree counter-question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 小叅舉香嚴上樹公案師云曾為浪子偏憐客潦倒香嚴指路殷緊夾籓籬寬闢道不知何自入無門
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yulin Tongxiu, in the Recorded Sayings of National Teacher Puji Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄), explicitly raises ‘Xiangyan up the tree’ as a public case during a small convocation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 德乃舉香嚴上樹話曰：『是何意旨？』余曰：『香嚴老漢弄巧成拙。』德曰：『他未上樹時又作麼生？』余便喝，德打一竹篦
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dabei Miaoyun (大悲妙雲禪師語錄), Miaoyun's autobiographical account. Miaoyun names his examiner as Chan Master Lingyin Jude Li (靈隱具德禮禪師). Jude Li raises the Xiangyan-up-the-tree case, presses Miaoyun about before the ascent, and strikes him with the bamboo comb. Miaoyun is the first-person respondent and later narrator, not the headword-bearing speaker.
